merger_name: Calvary – 14 Healthscope hospitals and Healthscope Independence Services

other_parties.name: LITTLE COMPANY OF MARY HEALTH CARE LIMITED

merger_description:
Little Company of Mary Health Care Ltd (**Calvary**), through a wholly owned subsidiary, proposes to acquire 14 private hospitals, together with Healthscope Independence Services and all head office and centralised corporate support functions from Healthscope (the **Acquisition**).   

  

As part of the Acquisition, Calvary will acquire the following hospitals:

* In New South Wales: Norwest Private, Lady Davidson Private, The Hills Private, and Sydney Clinic (all in Sydney), and Newcastle Private and Hunter Valley Private.
* In Victoria: John Fawkner Private, Melbourne Private, Melbourne Clinic, and Dorset Rehabilitation (all in Melbourne).
* In Queensland: Brisbane Private and Peninsula Private (both in Brisbane).
* In the Northern Territory: Darwin Private.
* In South Australia: Griffith Rehabilitation.

Calvary will also acquire Healthscope Independence Services, which offers special accommodation and care support services, including operating 10 supported independent living sites in Victoria, 2 in the Northern Territory and 1 in NSW.  

  

The Acquisition forms part of a broader consortium acquisition of Healthscope's portfolio. The other consortium members are Acurio Health, Healthe Care and KnG Group, which will each acquire separate hospitals pursuant to inter-conditional sale agreements.  

  

Calvary is a not-for-profit operator of private and publicly funded hospitals in Australia. Calvary currently operates thirteen hospitals, consisting of three publicly funded hospitals in Melbourne (Calvary Bethlehem), Sydney (Calvary Kogarah) and Newcastle (Calvary Mater), and ten private hospitals across the ACT, New South Wales, South Australia and Tasmania. Calvary also offers aged care and in-home aged care services.  

  

Healthscope is Australia's second-largest private hospital operator. On 26 May 2025, Healthscope's parent entities entered into receivership, with McGrathNicol appointed as Receivers to complete a sale of the business. The Receivers conducted an extended sale process over Healthscope's hospital portfolio.

Separate agreements were entered into between Calvary entities, Healthscope and the Receivers in December 2025 concerning the acquisition two additional Healthscope private hospitals – Holmesglen Private Hospital (Melbourne, Victoria) and Hobart Private Hospital (Hobart, Tasmania). The ACCC has considered each of these acquisitions previously and, in both cases, determined under section 51ABZE(1) that Calvary’s acquisition of the relevant hospital may be put into effect – see Calvary - Holmesglen Private Hospital (determination dated 28 April 2026) and Calvary - Hobart Private Hospital  (determination dated 27 August 2026).

events.title: Calvary – 14 Healthscope hospitals and Healthscope Independence Services - Phase 1 determination

determination_table_content.details: The reasons for the ACCC’s determination are set out in section 2.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines and interim merger process guidelines.

In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered the information and documents that were submitted with the notification form, additional information provided by the parties to the Acquisition, information provided by third parties and market feedback.
For the reasons given below, the ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into effect.
Background
Voluntary administration of Healthscope and consortium acquisition

In May 2025, Healthscope’s parent entities went into voluntary administration, and receivers (Receivers) and administrators were appointed by its lenders and the Healthscope Board respectively to conduct an orderly sale of the hospitals in its network. The Receivers conducted an extended sale process over Healthscope's hospital portfolio.

The Acquisition forms part of a broader consortium acquisition of Healthscope's portfolio, following the Receivers’ sale process. The other members of the consortium are Acurio Health, Healthe Care and KnG Group, which each propose to acquire separate hospitals pursuant to inter-conditional sale agreements.
Calvary’s private hospital service offering

Calvary operates in accordance with the Code of Ethical Standards for Catholic Health and Aged Care Services in Australia (Catholic Code). This means that certain services are generally not offered at Calvary’s facilities, including in vitro fertilisation (IVF) and other assisted reproductive services, voluntary assisted dying, elective terminations of pregnancy, and gender reassignment procedures.
Calvary’s provision of transitional Corporate Backbone services to other operators of Healthscope hospitals

The central focus of the ACCC’s assessment of this Acquisition has been Calvary’s proposed acquisition of the 14 Healthscope hospitals. However, as noted in section 1, as part of the Acquisition, Calvary would also acquire Healthscope’s Corporate Backbone, being the centralised head office and shared services functions that have historically supported Healthscope’s hospital portfolio.

Following completion of the Acquisition, Calvary would, via the Corporate Backbone, provide transitional services for a limited time to Healthscope (in respect of hospitals where Healthscope will continue to deliver services, including those not yet sold yet through the Receivers’ sale process), and other parties acquiring Healthscope hospitals.

The purpose of Calvary providing these transitional services to other parties would be to ensure that the central services provided by the Corporate Backbone continue to be delivered while each party completes its separation activities and establishes replacement services.
Relevant areas of competition
Horizontal overlap in the supply of private hospital services to patients, visiting medical officers and private health insurers in various areas

As identified in section 1, the Target Hospitals are located across Sydney, the Hunter region (in New South Wales), Melbourne, Brisbane, Darwin and Adelaide. In these regions, Calvary currently operates the following private hospitals:

items.text: In Adelaide: Calvary Adelaide Hospital, Calvary North Adelaide Hospital and Calvary Central Districts Hospital.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: Calvary does not currently operate any hospitals in Queensland or the Northern Territory. While Calvary operates one private hospital in New South Wales (Calvary Riverina Hospital in Wagga Wagga), it does not operate any private hospitals in Sydney or the Hunter region, where the Target Hospitals are located.

As a result, based on the material before it, the ACCC considers that Calvary only overlaps to varying degrees with the Target Hospitals located in Melbourne and Adelaide, in the supply of private hospital services in areas surrounding those Target Hospitals, specifically:

items.text: the supply of medical, surgical and emergency care services across a range of medical specialties to patients;
the supply of private hospital facilities, equipment and support staff to visiting medical officers (VMOs); and
the supply of Hospital Purchaser Provider Agreements to private health insurers.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: Limited overlap between Calvary and Healthscope Independence Services

Healthscope Independence Services (HIS) is a disability support service business comprising residential care services (including the provision of supported independent living sites and specialist disability accommodation sites) and attendant care services (including home services, personal care services, community services and rehabilitation support services).

Calvary offers aged care and in-home aged care services. However, based on the materials before it, the ACCC finds that there is limited overlap between these services and HIS’s residential care and attendant care services, because:

items.text: Calvary currently does not offer any disability-focused accommodation services; and

while (i) aged care and in-home aged care services and (ii) disability residential care and attendant care services both involve the supply of nursing services, the funding sources and client bases are different, such that these services are unlikely to be substitutable.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: Competition assessment

The ACCC has considered the effects of the Acquisition by comparing the likely future state of competition if the Acquisition proceeds against the likely future state of competition if the Acquisition does not proceed.

The ACCC has considered whether the Acquisition is likely to substantially lessen competition in the supply of private hospital services to patients, VMOs or private health insurers in any relevant market.

For the purpose of its assessment, it was not necessary to reach a definitive view on the precise product or geographic boundaries of the relevant market, as it does not materially alter the ACCC’s competition assessment.

The ACCC considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the effect of substantially lessening competition in the supply of private hospital services to patients, VMOs or private health insurers in any relevant market relative to the future without the Acquisition.
Based on information provided by the Parties and by third parties, the ACCC makes the following findings:

items.text: In the areas where Calvary overlaps with the Target Hospitals in the supply of private hospital services, the degree of overlap is small, as the relevant hospitals have largely different geographical catchment zones for patients and limited overlap of VMOs.
There is no real commercial likelihood of an alternative purchaser acquiring the Target Hospitals.

In the absence of a commercially realistic alternative purchaser, and in the context of Healthscope’s voluntary administration, there is not a real prospect that the Target Hospitals would continue operating as private hospitals in the future without the Acquisition.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: The ACCC has had regard to concerns received from several third parties regarding certain services currently provided at some of the Target Hospitals, which Calvary would likely not provide if the Acquisition proceeds, given that Calvary operates in accordance with the Catholic Code. These include certain IVF and other assisted reproductive services, voluntary assisted dying, elective terminations of pregnancy, and gender reassignment procedures (Relevant Services).

However, as noted above, the ACCC finds there is not a real prospect that the Target Hospitals would continue operating as private hospitals in the future without the Acquisition. Accordingly, the ACCC considers that the Relevant Services would likely cease being provided at the relevant Target Hospitals in both the future with and without the Acquisition.

The ACCC has also had regard to concerns raised by several third parties that, in the course of providing time-limited transitional services to other operators of Healthscope hospitals via the Corporate Backbone, Calvary may gain access to and use commercially sensitive information relating to third party hospitals, which may lead to reduced competition in the supply of private hospital services. However, having regard to the time-limited nature of the transitional arrangements, the ACCC considers that these arrangements are unlikely to substantially lessen competition.
